description: A four-panel composite figure of experimental and simulated flow-stress curves for low-alloy steel. All panels share identical axes — Stress (MPa) from 45 to 90 on the ordinate (gridlines at 45, 60, 75, 90) and True strain from 0 to 0.9 in steps of 0.1 on the abscissa — and each is annotated "Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹". (a) and (b) show the decreasing-temperature tests; the top-right legend reads "1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)" (magenta) and "1050°C-950°C(0.4 strain)" (light blue), and the lower legend gives solid "Experimental" and dashed open-circle "Simulated (Model 1)" in (a) versus "Simulated (Model 2)" in (b). (c) and (d) repeat the layout for increasing temperature with legend "950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)" (magenta) and "950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)" (light blue), Model 1 in (c) and Model 2 in (d). Annotation labels "950°C" and "1050°C" mark the two isothermal reference curves, the 1050°C reference lying lowest (≈46–57 MPa). In (a)/(b) the temperature drop produces a second hardening peak near 70 MPa for the 0.2-strain case and a lower second peak near 66 MPa for 0.4 strain; in (c)/(d) the temperature rise produces strong softening toward ≈48 MPa. The figure demonstrates that Model 2 reproduces the transient softening better than Model 1.

subfigures.description: Stress (MPa) vs true strain at 0.01 s⁻¹ for the 1050°C→950°C tests, ε1 = 0.2 (magenta) and 0.4 (light blue); black solid = Experimental, black dashed with open circles = Simulated (Model 1). After the temperature drop at ε1 a second peak appears, higher for the 0.2-strain curve (near 70 MPa at strain ~0.3) than for the 0.4-strain curve (near 66 MPa at ~0.55). A black 1050°C reference (peak ≈57 MPa) and a high purple 950°C reference (peak near 84 MPa at strain ~0.15, rising again after 0.6) are also plotted and labelled by annotation.

Same axes, legend and colour scheme as (a) but the dashed open-circle curves are labelled 'Simulated (Model 2)'. The second-stage peaks of the magenta (0.2 strain) and light blue (0.4 strain) curves are at the same strains as in (a) but the simulated curves run closer to the experimental ones than in (a).

Stress vs true strain at 0.01 s⁻¹ for the 950°C→1050°C tests, ε1 = 0.2 (magenta) and 0.4 (light blue); black solid = Experimental, black dashed open circles = Simulated (Model 1). The experimental magenta curve peaks near 81 MPa at strain ~0.2 and then falls steeply to ≈48 MPa by strain ~0.5; the light-blue experimental curve peaks near 84 MPa and falls to ≈48 MPa by ~0.5. The Model 1 open-circle curves drop at clearly larger strain, i.e. the predicted softening is delayed. Black (1050°C) reference lies at ≈46–57 MPa and the purple 950°C reference at ≈70–84 MPa.

Identical layout to (c) but the dashed open-circle curves are 'Simulated (Model 2)'; the simulated magenta and light-blue curves now fall at nearly the same strain as the corresponding experimental curves, matching the softening transient more closely than Model 1 in (c).

observations.observation: All four panels plot Stress (MPa), axis 45–90, against True strain, axis 0–0.9, and carry the annotation 'Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹'.

Panel (a) legend lists '1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)' in magenta and '1050°C-950°C(0.4 strain)' in light blue; panel (c) legend lists '950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)' and '950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)' in the same colours.

In every panel a solid black curve is labelled 'Experimental' and a dashed black curve with open circles is labelled 'Simulated'; the model label is 'Simulated (Model 1)' in (a) and (c) and 'Simulated (Model 2)' in (b) and (d).
Annotation text '950°C' and '1050°C' labels the two isothermal reference curves present in all four panels; the 1050°C curve is the lowest, lying between roughly 46 and 57 MPa.

In (a) and (b) the 0.2-strain (magenta) experimental curve develops a second hardening peak near 70 MPa at true strain ≈0.3, while the 0.4-strain (light blue) curve develops a lower second peak near 66 MPa at true strain ≈0.55.

In (c) and (d) the magenta (0.2 strain) experimental curve peaks near 81 MPa at true strain ≈0.2 and then falls steeply to about 48 MPa, while the light-blue (0.4 strain) curve peaks near 84 MPa and falls to about 48 MPa.
In panel (c) the open-circle Model 1 simulated curves for both 0.2 and 0.4 strain drop at noticeably larger true strain than the matching experimental curves, i.e. the predicted softening is delayed.
In panel (d) the Model 2 open-circle curves fall at nearly the same true strain as the experimental curves, unlike the delayed Model 1 curves in (c).
The caption states that (a) and (c) correspond to simulation with Model 1 and (b) and (d) to simulation with Model 2.
The caption states the test conditions: strain rate 0.01 s⁻¹; (a)/(b) TI = 1050°C and TII = 950°C; (c)/(d) TI = 950°C and TII = 1050°C; with εI = 0.2 or 0.4.
The citing text states that for the decreasing-temperature case (Fig. 9a) the greater the strain at which the temperature began to decrease, the lower the peak stress level in the second stage.

The citing text states that the stress softening predicted by Model 1 was weaker than, and delayed relative to, the experimental findings in the decreasing-temperature (Fig. 9a) and increasing-temperature (Fig. 9c) cases.
The citing text states that Model 2 showed higher prediction accuracy for the stress softening caused by decreasing and increasing temperature at different εI (Fig. 9b and 9d) than Model 1.

unreadable_items: The purple high-stress and black low-stress isothermal reference curves are not listed in either legend; their identity as the 950 °C and 1050 °C isothermal references is inferred only from the '950°C' and '1050°C' annotation leaders.
The flat purple dashed segment at ≈72 MPa spanning roughly strain 0.55–0.9 in (a)/(b) has no legend entry and its way of being produced cannot be determined from the pixels.
No numeric peak-stress or steady-state-stress values are printed on any panel, so curve values can only be located relative to the 45/60/75/90 MPa gridlines.
